sourcedFrom: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Semi-Automatic Compact Pistol Cal. .380 ACP PD380 — Rev.A — back cover '8.505.82.02-06.2023 Rev.A' (2023 — back cover 'Copyright © 2023 · Carl WALTHER GmbH')
cleanIntro: The PD380 is a hammer-fired compact .380 ACP that fires double action or single action, with a manual safety and a takedown lever. Walther publishes one field strip for it — takedown lever down, slide forward off the frame, recoil guide rod out — and tells you never to go further. That makes this a short job with a clear boundary: everything the cleaning section asks for is reachable from those parts.

steps.title: Muzzle safe, finger out, magazine out
steps.action: Point the muzzle in a safe direction and keep your finger off the trigger and outside the trigger guard. Press the magazine release and take the magazine out of the grip before you touch the slide.
steps.prose: The order matters on any pistol and the book says why: release the slide with a loaded magazine in and you have chambered a new round. The PD380's magazine release is ambidextrous, so either side works. Do this first, every time, before anything else moves.
steps.quote: Point the muzzle in a safe direction. Make sure your finger is off the trigger and out of the trigger guard. Press the magazine release and remove the magazine (fig. 15).
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Semi-Automatic Compact Pistol Cal. .380 ACP PD380 — Rev.A — back cover '8.505.82.02-06.2023 Rev.A' — 7 Unloading the pistol, printed p.20 (PDF p.20)
steps.warn: ANY TIME YOU RELEASE THE SLIDE WHILE A MAGAZINE CONTAINING CARTRIDGES IS IN THE PISTOL, YOU WILL HAVE CHAMBERED A NEW ROUND IN THE PISTOL.

steps.title: Slide briskly to the rear, port unobstructed
steps.action: Grasp the serrated sides of the slide from the rear with your thumb and fingers and draw it briskly all the way back, so that any cartridge in the chamber is extracted and thrown clear. Keep your hand away from the ejection port while you do it.
steps.prose: Grip from above or behind, never in front of the muzzle. A hand cupped over the ejection port is the usual reason a round fails to clear — it catches the cartridge and drops it back where it came from.
steps.quote: Grasp the serrated sides of the slide from the rear with the thumb and fingers, and briskly draw the slide fully rearward in order to extract any cartridge from the chamber and clear it from the pistol.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Semi-Automatic Compact Pistol Cal. .380 ACP PD380 — Rev.A — back cover '8.505.82.02-06.2023 Rev.A' — 7 Unloading the pistol, printed p.20 (PDF p.20)

steps.title: Look into the chamber and down the magazine well
steps.action: Look into the chamber and down through the magazine well, and confirm no ammunition remains anywhere in the pistol. Then look down the bore for any obstruction.
steps.prose: The PD380 has a loaded chamber indicator at the upper rear of the ejection port, and the book is plain that it is not the check: light, dirt and tarnished brass can all hide what it shows. The surest check is the one in this step — magazine out, slide back, eyes on the chamber.
steps.quote: Visually check the barrel chamber to be sure it is empty. Look into the chamber and down through the magazine well. Verify that no ammunition remains in the pistol.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Semi-Automatic Compact Pistol Cal. .380 ACP PD380 — Rev.A — back cover '8.505.82.02-06.2023 Rev.A' — 7 Unloading the pistol, printed p.20 (PDF p.20)
steps.warn: NEVER RELY UPON THE LOADED CHAMBER INDICATOR ALONE TO VERIFY THE PRESENCE OR ABSENCE OF A ROUND IN THE CHAMBER.

steps.title: Lock it open on an empty magazine, then take the magazine out
steps.action: Push the emptied magazine back in and draw the slide back: it should lock in its rearmost position on the slide stop. Then take the empty magazine out again.
steps.prose: The slide stop is worked by the magazine follower, so the PD380 only locks open with an empty magazine in place — with no magazine at all you will have to hold the slide back yourself. Look into the chamber once more while it is open.
steps.quote: Insert the empty magazine, retract the slide. The slide should be locked back in its rearmost position by the slide stop
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Semi-Automatic Compact Pistol Cal. .380 ACP PD380 — Rev.A — back cover '8.505.82.02-06.2023 Rev.A' — 7 Unloading the pistol, printed p.20 (PDF p.20)

steps.title: Safety to SAFE, magazine out — before the takedown
steps.action: With the pistol unloaded and the muzzle in a safe direction, put the manual safety in the safe position and confirm the magazine is out. Walther's own section 3.2 defines the safe position: rotate the safety lever to the lower position.
steps.prose: This is Walther's own first line of the disassembly. Section 3.2 and its picture caption name the lever's lower position SAFE and the upper position FIRE; go by those. Wear safety glasses for the strip and the reassembly — the recoil spring is under pressure.
steps.caution: ALWAYS FOLLOW THE FIELD STRIPPING INSTRUCTIONS EXACTLY.
steps.quote: Keep the muzzle pointed in a safe direction, place manual safety in the safe position and remove the magazine (fig. 20).
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Semi-Automatic Compact Pistol Cal. .380 ACP PD380 — Rev.A — back cover '8.505.82.02-06.2023 Rev.A' — 9.1 Disassembling, printed p.23 (PDF p.23)

steps.title: Takedown lever straight down
steps.action: Pull the takedown lever straight down, and keep holding it down.
steps.prose: Straight down is the whole instruction — the book does not ask you to turn it or press anything else. Do not let go of it yet: the next step takes the slide off while the lever is still held.
steps.quote: Pull the takedown lever straight down (fig. 21).
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Semi-Automatic Compact Pistol Cal. .380 ACP PD380 — Rev.A — back cover '8.505.82.02-06.2023 Rev.A' — 9.1 Disassembling, printed p.23 (PDF p.23)

steps.title: Slide forward and off the frame, lever still held
steps.action: Still holding the takedown lever down, move the slide forward and take it off the front of the frame.
steps.prose: Control the slide with your hand behind the muzzle, never in front of it. If the slide will not move forward with the lever held down, stop rather than force it — the book gives no other way off.
steps.quote: Move the slide forward, and remove it from the frame (fig. 22) while still holding the takedown lever.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Semi-Automatic Compact Pistol Cal. .380 ACP PD380 — Rev.A — back cover '8.505.82.02-06.2023 Rev.A' — 9.1 Disassembling, printed p.23 (PDF p.23)

steps.title: Recoil guide rod out from under the barrel, spring under control
steps.action: Turn the slide over and remove the recoil guide rod assembly from below the barrel, taking up the spring pressure with your thumb as it comes free.
steps.prose: The spring is still compressed when the slide comes off, so let it out slowly rather than letting it jump. Note which way round the assembly sat under the barrel — it goes back the same way.
steps.quote: Remove the recoil guide rod assembly from below the barrel while taking up the spring pressure (fig. 23).
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Semi-Automatic Compact Pistol Cal. .380 ACP PD380 — Rev.A — back cover '8.505.82.02-06.2023 Rev.A' — 9.1 Disassembling, printed p.23 (PDF p.23)

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Lay out the main components as the book pictures them: the recoil guide rod, the frame with grip, the barrel, the slide and the magazine. That is the whole of the disassembly Walther publishes for the PD380.
steps.prose: The book forbids going past this point, and any maintenance not specified in it goes to a qualified gunsmith using genuine Walther parts. The book's text names no separate step for lifting the barrel out of the slide; this guide does not add one.
steps.caution: NEVER DISASSEMBLE YOUR HANDGUN beyond the field stripping procedure outlined in this manual.
steps.quote: The main components of the pistol are shown in (fig. 19).
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Semi-Automatic Compact Pistol Cal. .380 ACP PD380 — Rev.A — back cover '8.505.82.02-06.2023 Rev.A' — 9.1 Disassembling, printed p.23 (PDF p.23)

steps.title: Bore from the chamber end, brush all the way through
steps.action: Starting from the chamber end, push a brass-bristle bore brush wet with a good powder-removing solvent through the bore until the bristles come fully out of the muzzle, then draw it back until they come fully out of the chamber end. Wipe the bore clean with patches or a swab.
steps.prose: Letting the bristles clear the bore completely before reversing is what keeps them from bending back inside the barrel. On a new pistol the book also asks for the factory preservative to be wiped from the bore, chamber and exposed areas before first use.
steps.quote: Starting with the barrel and from chamber end, insert a brush through the bore of the barrel until the bristles completely exit at muzzle end.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Semi-Automatic Compact Pistol Cal. .380 ACP PD380 — Rev.A — back cover '8.505.82.02-06.2023 Rev.A' — 9.2 Cleaning, printed p.24 (PDF p.24)

steps.title: Breech face, extractor and the frame
steps.action: With a small brush dipped in solvent, take all deposits off the breech face, the chamber end of the barrel, the extractor and the areas around them that see powder and primer residue. Brush the frame lightly with solvent to lift its residue.
steps.prose: These are the surfaces that take the gas and the primer spit, and the extractor is the one that decides whether a case comes out — give it its own attention with the small brush.
steps.quote: Using a small brush dipped in solvent, remove all deposits from around the breech face, chamber end of the barrel, extractor and adjacent areas which have been exposed to powder or primer residue.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Semi-Automatic Compact Pistol Cal. .380 ACP PD380 — Rev.A — back cover '8.505.82.02-06.2023 Rev.A' — 9.2 Cleaning, printed p.24 (PDF p.24)

steps.title: Oil by the drop, at the points the book names
steps.action: Barrel: a light film on all its external surfaces and on the ramp where the locking block cams it. Frame: one drop on the slide guides and one on the trigger bar. Slide: one drop on the safety plunger and one on the disconnector cut. Magazine: a light film on its external metal surfaces.
steps.prose: Walther's figure 24 marks these points A to F, and "only one drop" means one. Over-oiling attracts dirt, unburned powder and carbon. In a cold climate use a lubricant that will not congeal.
steps.quote: Put only one drop of lubricant on the slide guides [C], and on the trigger bar [D].
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Semi-Automatic Compact Pistol Cal. .380 ACP PD380 — Rev.A — back cover '8.505.82.02-06.2023 Rev.A' — 9.3 Lubrication, printed p.25 (PDF p.25)
steps.warn: Do not put any gun lubricant into the striker channel.

steps.title: Check for wear every time
steps.action: Every time you clean the pistol, look it over for signs of wear. If you find wear, do not use it: return it to Walther for service or have it checked by a qualified gunsmith.
steps.prose: The book sets this as part of every clean, not an occasional inspection.
steps.quote: Every time you clean the firearm, check it for signs of wear. If wear is noted, do not use the firearm.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Semi-Automatic Compact Pistol Cal. .380 ACP PD380 — Rev.A — back cover '8.505.82.02-06.2023 Rev.A' — 9.4 Maintenance before Storing, printed p.25 (PDF p.25)

deepAbsentReason: Walther's PD380 book publishes one field strip (9.1 Disassembling, printed p.23: takedown lever down, slide forward off the frame, recoil guide rod out) and nothing past it. It tells the owner never to disassemble the handgun beyond that procedure (printed p.8) and sends any maintenance or service not in the manual to a qualified gunsmith using genuine Walther parts (11 Repair of Walther pistols, printed p.27). There is no deeper published procedure, so none is invented here.

cleaning.name: BORE
tasks: Brass-bristle bore brush and a good powder-removing solvent, from the chamber end
Bristles fully out at the muzzle before drawing back, fully out at the chamber end before pushing again
Bore wiped clean with patches or a swab
New pistol: factory oil wiped from the bore, chamber and exposed areas before first use

cleaning.name: BREECH & FRAME
tasks: Small brush and solvent around the breech face
Chamber end of the barrel and the extractor cleaned of powder and primer residue

cleaning.name: LUBRICATION
tasks: Barrel: light film on all external surfaces and on the locking-block cam ramp
Frame: one drop on the slide guides, one on the trigger bar
Slide: one drop on the safety plunger, one on the disconnector cut
Magazine: light film on the external metal surfaces
All external metal surfaces filmed and wiped clean
⛔ No lubricant into the striker channel
Do not over-lubricate: nothing dripping or running down the pistol

cleaning.name: STORAGE
tasks: Unloaded, with the safety in the safe position
Never kept in leather or heavy cloth that holds moisture
Long storage: bore, chamber and internal working mechanism lubricated; slide, barrel and magazine coated against corrosion
Cleaned again before the pistol is next used

reassembly: Walther's PD380 book prints no reassembly procedure. What follows is the field strip in reverse and nothing more; if any part will not go back as it came off, stop and contact Walther.
Recoil guide rod assembly back in below the barrel, the same way round it came out, controlling the spring as it seats.
Slide back onto the frame from the front and drawn fully rearward; the takedown lever ends where it was before you pulled it down.
Safety glasses on for the reassembly, as the book asks for every assembly and disassembly.
fncheck: Walther's functional inspection (4.2, printed pp.15–16), on the empty pistol with the muzzle in a safe direction: remove the magazine and retract the slide — when released, the recoil spring returns it fully forward into battery. Insert the empty magazine and retract the slide — it locks back in its rearmost position on the slide stop. Remove the magazine, pull the slide back slightly and release it — it returns fully forward into battery. Finally check the manual safety moves between its lower (SAFE) and upper (FIRE) positions, and store the pistol with it in SAFE.
